patch_description:
This program replaces the short, height-restricted lookahead with a priority-aware rollout policy.

The key idea is that moving a blocking suffix onto a stack does not only affect stack height: it buries every box already in the destination stack. Burying a box that will be needed soon is much more harmful than burying a large-label box that will only be needed far later. The new implementation therefore uses an obstruction potential based on the labels currently contained in each candidate destination stack.

For every real move, all possible destination stacks are evaluated. Each candidate is simulated through a substantially longer deterministic rollout. During that rollout, future suffix moves are selected using the priority-weighted burial potential, and the remaining state receives a terminal penalty for near-future boxes that are still deeply buried. This combines exact local simulation with a label-aware estimate of delayed extraction cost.

The algorithm remains safely within the operation limit: every box is removed once and each box causes at most one suffix-moving operation before its removal.
